title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-taylor-hughes
content:
Quick debugging scratchpad for recurring GPU OOM / driver mismatch issues observed on staging and a couple of Dedicated nodes. Mostly a brain dump of commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses and next steps.

Encounter summary:
- Symptom: intermittent CUDA OOMs during long-running chat generation workloads (mostly with long context + sampling). Some instances show explicit driver/runtime mismatch errors.
- Affected: staging-gpu-02, dedicated-pool-node-7 (NVIDIA A40s), also one customer on Dedicated reported similar.
- First noticed after we rolled a new container built with CUDA toolkit 12.1 (image: rw-inference/base:py310-cuda12.1).

Commands & outputs captured:
1) nvidia-smi (host)
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 510.47       Driver Version: 510.47       CUDA Version: 11.2     |
|-------------------------------+----------------------+----------------------+

Note: host driver reports 510.47 (CUDA 11.2). Container image was built with CUDA 12 toolchain -> potential mismatch.

2) inside container checks:
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
2.2.0
11.7
True

Observation: PyTorch was built against CUDA 11.7 (in image), host driver shows CUDA 11.2 capability. This can cause runtime issues ("cuda driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version").

3) Example runtime error from logs (staging-gpu-02, 2024-02-10 03:22:11):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "generate.py", line 214, in <module>
    res = model.generate(inputs)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate(handle)`

4) Another log showing explicit mismatch (from dedicated-pool-node-7 container startup):
2024-02-27T10:11:05Z ERROR runtime: failed to initialize CUDA runtime: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
Caused by: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory

5) PyTorch OOM example (captured by app):
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 48.00 GiB total capacity; 46.50 GiB already allocated; 1.20 GiB free; 49.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
Suggested action in-app: reduce batch size or enable caching.

Commands tried (what I ran and results):
- Verified driver on host: sudo nvidia-smi -> driver 510.47.
- Checked kernel modules: lsmod | grep nvidia -> nvidia, nvidia_uvm present.
- Restarted nvidia-persistenced: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced -> small improvement in allocation turnaround but not root cause.
- Rebooted node dedicated-pool-node-7 -> temporarily resolved the CUBLAS_ALLOC failures once, reappeared under load.
- Confirmed libcuda visible inside container: ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcuda.so* -> file missing in some containers (we rely on host-provided libcuda via /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu).
- Verified container run flags: docker run --gpus all --runtime=nvidia ... (we run via k8s with device-plugin).
- pip show torch / conda list to confirm mismatch between installed torch build and host driver.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver / CUDA runtime mismatch: container/toolkit (12.x) or torch binary built against newer CUDA than host driver supports -> leads to "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" and allocation failures.
2) Memory fragmentation / long-lived cache: KV cache + many concurrent requests causing fragmentation and allocation failures despite enough nominal free memory. (CUBLAS_ALLOC failures are often symptomatic of fragmentation).
3) Bug in our batching logic or not clearing cuda cache between requests in long-lived process -> memory retention.
4) Host-level driver bug for specific driver version 510.47 interacting poorly with A40 firmware; upgrade/downgrade may be needed.

Mitigations attempted (short-term):
- Reduced per-request max_new_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 for affected workloads (immediately reduced frequency of OOMs).
- Explicit torch.cuda.empty_cache() at end of generation loop (minor effect).
- Forced whole-process restart on OOM via k8s liveness probe (workaround only).
- Tried running image built with older CUDA 11.2 libs -> matched host driver and the "insufficient driver" error disappeared.

Longer-term actions / notes for ops & infra:
- Either upgrade host driver to a recent branch that supports CUDA 12.x toolchain (preferred for new images) OR pin images to CUDA 11.2/11.7 builds for the Dedicated fleet. Need decision.
  - Driver upgrade path: target NVIDIA driver >= 535.x to safely support CUDA 12.1 runtime images. Test matrix required: 535.x vs 530.x on A40 cluster.
  - If pinning images: rebuild base images with CUDA 11.2 toolchain (or use torch wheel built for 11.2) and deploy to staging + dedicated.
- Add preflight probe in rollout: container sanity check script that runs python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')" to detect libcuda visibility and basic mismatch before marking pod Ready.
- Increase observability: capture nvidia-smi + torch.cuda.memory_summary() on OOM and ship to logs for postmortem.
- Add auto-retry/backoff in our request router when a node exhibits repeated cublas/cudnn allocation failures (temporary drain).

Notes from discussion with SRE (2024-02-28):
- SRE saw that our k8s nodes had driver 510 due to older AMI; plan to test 525/535 in a canary ASG.
- They recommended mounting host libcuda to container via --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 if using custom base images that don't include it. But this is brittle across distros.

Repro steps to test locally (dev machine with single A100):
1) Build container with CUDA 12.1 image and run on host with older driver -> expect error: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version".
2) Run same container after downgrading torch wheel to one built for CUDA 11.7 or 11.2. Should remove mismatch.
3) Synthetic fragmentation test: allocate many small tensors and free them repeatedly, then try to allocate a large tensor: observe cublas alloc failure if fragmentation severe.

Raw error snippets collected (for logs / search):
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate(handle)`"
- "libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate ..."

Open questions / next steps:
- Decision: upgrade host driver to support CUDA12 images vs pin images to CUDA11.x. Which path has lower operational risk? (Ops action item).
- Can we add runtime preflight check in CI for images that will run on Dedicated fleet? Who owns implementing this? (assign to devexp / infra).
- Investigate memory fragmentation hypothesis further: reproduce fragment case and instrument allocation pattern in runtime. (assign to eng-serving-runtime: Elena + Taylor).
- Run driver compatibility matrix on a canary group of nodes (SRE).

References / useful links:
- NVIDIA docs: "CUDA driver/runtime version compatibility"
- Internal ticket ENG-1234 (linked above)
- PR with quick preflight probe: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482

TL;DR: Most likely cause is driver/runtime mismatch for a subset of images we deployed. Immediate mitigations: pin images to host-supported CUDA or upgrade drivers on nodes. Also need better preflight detection and more granular OOM instrumentation.

-- Taylor (notes)
